name: Connect two tables — the four kinds

tables.name: authors
tables.comment: One row per person who wrote something we sell.

columns.name: country
columns.comment: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Nullable: we often do not know.

tables.name: books
tables.comment: One row per edition we stock. author_id is now a real foreign key into authors.

columns.name: author_id
columns.comment: The referencing (child) side of the foreign key into authors.id.

columns.name: isbn
columns.comment: The natural key. UNIQUE, but not the primary key.

columns.name: contributors_json
columns.comment: Denormalized snapshot of this edition's contributors, embedded so a page render needs no join. contributors stays the source of truth; see the Kind: Serialized connection below.

tables.name: contributors
tables.comment: Illustrators, translators and editors credited besides the author of record.

tables.name: book_stats
tables.comment: Fed by a nightly rollup, not a constraint. See the Data flow connection from books.

columns.name: book_id
columns.comment: Not a foreign key: this table is fed by a data flow, not constrained by one.

tables.name: catalog_export
tables.comment: Nightly feed pushed to the retailer catalog API. Reads books; nothing here is a foreign key.

relationships.name: books_author_id_fkey
relationships.note: belongs-to usually pairs with ON DELETE CASCADE, but a deleted author should not silently erase sales history: RESTRICT until someone reassigns or removes the books by hand.

relationships.name: contributors snapshot
relationships.note: Denormalized on purpose: a book page reads books alone. contributors is still a real table for the roster itself.

relationships.name: nightly stats rollup
relationships.note: Nightly job, not a constraint: dropping a book does not touch its stale book_stats row.

relationships.name: reads books nightly
relationships.note: Nothing enforces this. Dropping books would silently break the export job with no constraint violation to warn you.

notes.text:
Kind decides what the database does; the verb only changes the sentence.

fk — real FOREIGN KEY, in the DDL, joinable in Trace, needs a column pair.
flow — dashed, a comment only, never DDL, not joinable, no columns needed.
embed — solid diamond, a comment only, needs exactly one column: the one holding the serialized rows.
dependency — dotted, a comment only, no columns, no rows move.

Every verb is stored source → target. "Has", "contains" and "used by" are just belongs-to, part-of and uses read backwards — that is why they need no connection of their own.
